title: What Is an API Gateway?
sources: microservices.io, 'Pattern: API Gateway / Backends for Frontends' (microservices.io/patterns/apigateway): the API gateway is the single entry point for all clients; it routes requests to the appropriate service and may also handle authentication and other edge functions

IBM, 'What is an API gateway?' (ibm.com/think/topics/api-gateway): an API gateway sits between clients and backend services, accepts API calls, routes them to the right service, and handles cross-cutting tasks like authentication, rate limiting and monitoring

AWS Prescriptive Guidance, 'API gateway pattern' (docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/modernization-integrating-microservices/api-gateway-pattern.html): a gateway provides one entry point that routes client requests to microservices

Gravitee, 'Ensuring API gateway against the risk of single point of failure' (gravitee.io/blog/ensuring-api-gateway-against-risk-single-point-failure-spof): a single gateway is a single point of failure; run multiple gateway instances behind a load balancer for high availability

lines.text: Your app is now ten small services,
so which one does your phone actually call?
You don't wander the halls looking for the chef,
you just ask the front desk.
one front door for every service.
Your phone sends every request there,
and it passes each one to the right service.
It also checks your ID first,
and turns away anyone knocking too often.
But if that one door breaks, nobody gets in,
so big apps run several copies of it.
One door in, many rooms behind it.
